title: Contradictory CSM Commitments Surface at Renewal
scenario_text:
**CRM — Account: Praxis Consulting Group**
ARR: $198K | Health Score: 71 (Yellow) | Renewal date: July 15, 2026 | CSM History: @elena.voss (Jan 2025 - Aug 2025), @aisha.patel (Sep 2025 - present) | Opportunity: 'Praxis Renewal FY27' Stage: Negotiation | Notes (by Aisha, last week): 'Customer insisting on locked pricing for 2 years. Says Elena promised this verbally during onboarding.'

**Zendesk — Ticket #49877 (Open)**
Subject: 'Renewal pricing dispute' | Customer comment (Praxis COO, Marta Ibarra): 'We were explicitly told by our previous CSM that our rate would be locked for the first 2 renewal cycles as part of the enterprise commitment. This was a condition of us signing. Please honor this.'

**Slack — #customer-success (Legacy workspace — meridian-2024.slack.com)**
[Thread from Feb 2025, found via search]
@elena.voss: Quick Q — Praxis is asking for a 2-year rate lock as a signing condition. Can we do that?
@david.okafor (then-VP CS, now at another company): We don't normally but for $200K+ deals it's been done. Check with deal desk.
@elena.voss: Deal desk said no formal mechanism. Can I just confirm verbally and we'll figure it out at renewal?
@david.okafor: :+1:
[End of thread]

**Google Doc — 'Praxis Onboarding Kickoff Notes' (Created: Jan 15, 2025, by @elena.voss)**
Attendees: Elena Voss, Marta Ibarra (COO), two Praxis engineers
Section: 'Agreed Terms'
- Implementation timeline: 6 weeks
- Dedicated support channel
- 'Pricing: locked per agreement'
[No further detail on duration or formal reference]

**CRM — Contract Object: Praxis Consulting Group**
MSA signed: Jan 10, 2025 | Term: 12 months, auto-renew | Pricing clause: 'Standard annual adjustment per published rate card, not to exceed 7% annually.' | No addendum referencing rate lock.

**Confluence — 'Deal Desk Pricing Exceptions' (Current page, last updated Mar 2026)**
Section 2: 'Rate locks exceeding 12 months require VP Sales + CFO co-approval and must be documented as a contract addendum. Verbal commitments are not binding per company policy (see Legal Advisory 2025-003).'

**Slack — DM between @aisha.patel and @elena.voss (Oct 2025, when Aisha took over)**
@aisha.patel: Hey! Taking over Praxis. Anything I should know?
@elena.voss: Great account. Marta is super engaged. Only thing — I may have soft-committed to a rate lock situation. Didn't get it in writing but they'll probably bring it up at renewal. Sorry :grimacing:
@aisha.patel: reacted with :woman-facepalming:
question: What is Meridian's actual obligation regarding Praxis's pricing at renewal, and what should Aisha recommend?

contributor.name: Aisha Patel
contributor.title: Senior Customer Success Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Enterprise account management, renewal strategy, cross-functional coordination

choices: Escalate to legal — the conflicting evidence between the verbal commitment and the written contract creates liability risk that only legal can resolve.
Honor the 2-year rate lock — Elena's verbal commitment, the VP's Slack approval, and the kickoff doc constitute a binding agreement. Process as-is with no price increase.
Offer a 1-year rate lock as compromise — there's enough evidence of intent to warrant partial accommodation, but not a full 2-year commitment. Escalate to current VP CS for approval.
No obligation exists — the MSA explicitly allows annual adjustment up to 7%, no addendum was filed, and company policy states verbal commitments are non-binding. Apply standard pricing.
